podcast.body: Featured on the 1991 album "Nevermind," this song became the second single released from the album. Its distinctive guitar riff drew similarities to Killing Joke's 1985 song "80s," prompting concerns from Kurt Cobain about what Killing Joke's frontman, Jazz Coleman, might think. The ensuing controversy in 1992 threatened to disrupt the song's release as a single and potentially interrupt the overall momentum of "Nevermind." "Still, back in 1992, the whole controversy threatened to scuttle Come As You Are, which was released as the second single from Never Mind."
